title: Why some restrict, others extend praedestinatio — creation not under mercy-end
source_text: XXXVII. Quod si quis ulterius quaerat, unde sit ut Theologi alii sic restringant, alii vero sic extendant praedestinationis vocem? Respondeo hoc inde esse quod alii plures, alii pauciores divinae providentiae actus atque effectus referunt ad finem a Deo intentum in quorundam hominum praedestinatione, qui est illustratio misericordiae divinae in eorum salute. In hoc enim Theologi consentire videntur, quod ad praedestinationem & reprobationem hominum revocandi sunt omnes providentiae Dei actus atque effectus, qui ad manifestationem tum misericordiae, tum justitiae divinae in certorum hominum vel aeterna salute, vel justa punitione per se referuntur. Finem autem illum a Deo intentum in hominis creatione, alii negant, alii affirmant. Juxta hos posteriores aeternum Dei decretum de homine condendo praedestinationis decretum ingreditur, & partem illius facit, minime vero, secundum priorum sententiam, ad quam accedimus ut probabilorem. Quippe hominis creatio per se & directe referri non videtur ad misericordiae vel justitiae divinae manifestationem, sed potius ad illustrationem potentiae, bonitatis, & sapientiae divinae.
pass_a_gloss: But if anyone ask further whence it is that some Theologians so restrict, others so extend, the word praedestinatio? I answer that this is because some refer more, others fewer, acts and effects of divine providence to the end intended by God in the predestination of certain men, which is the illustration of divine mercy in their salvation. For in this the Theologians seem to agree: that to the predestination and reprobation of men are to be recalled all acts and effects of God’s providence which of themselves are referred to the manifestation of both divine mercy and justice in the eternal salvation or just punishment of certain men. But that end intended by God in man’s creation some deny, others affirm. According to these latter the eternal decree of God concerning creating man enters the decree of predestination and makes a part of it; not so, according to the opinion of the former, to which we come as the more probable. For man’s creation does not seem of itself and directly to be referred to the manifestation of divine mercy or justice, but rather to the illustration of divine power, goodness, and wisdom.
pass_b_english: Why restrict vs extend praedestinatio? How many providence-acts they tie to the mercy-end in election.
Agreed: acts/effects that of themselves show mercy or justice in salvation/punishment belong under election/reprobation.
Disputed: whether creation’s end is that mercy/justice end.
Extenders: create-man decree enters praedestinatio; restrictors (Le Blanc, more probable): it does not.
Creation → power, goodness, wisdom — not directly mercy/justice manifestation.
